correctness.rationale: Reflection decomposition gives a dark Hamiltonian and a strictly stable bright amplitude matrix. The projected dephasing form has real part <= -1/2, with equality only for the dark identity after imposing the Hamiltonian-frequency condition, so the simple real leading eigenbranch has first coefficient -1/2. A stable Lyapunov equation determines the second coefficient; the manuscript writes an explicit Hermitian matrix and verifies its boundary and interior entries symbolically, giving c=L/(4*kappa)+kappa*(L+1)*(L+2)/(192*g*g). Dissipativity excludes any Re(eigenvalue)=0 for every gamma>0. Direct dense finite-spectra and Lyapunov-solver comparisons corroborate 32+36 instances but are not the general proof. Hypotheses, normalization and non-uniform remainder scope are explicit.

value.rationale: Weak dephasing of interference-protected transport is a natural challenge in sink-coupled quantum networks; an exact escape exponent determines metastable survival rather than only ultimate absorption. The universal gamma/2 slope and fully explicit second-order size/capture/hopping dependence distinguish competing processes and give a reusable path-wide analytic benchmark. The exact bright Lyapunov inversion is substantive structure beyond generic perturbation formalism and beyond already known inverse-gamma order-of-magnitude estimates. This is not a finite table recomputation or a routine substitution.
